primitives.name: Player-Team Heterogeneous Interaction Graph Transformer
primitives.verbatim_quote: Transformer: extends TokenGT [31] — |V|+|E| tokens into a standard transformer with Laplacian-eigenvector node identifiers (extended for direction) and three trainable embeddings (node type P_A, edge type P_K, node identifiers P_V); edge augmentation [X_E, P_u - P_v + P_k]; node augmentation [X_V, P_v + P_v + P_a].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{Z}_{\\text{node}}': 'Node embedding vector space (dimension 16)', '\\mathcal{X}_V': 'Node feature matrix (players/team nodes)', '\\mathcal{X}_E': 'Edge feature matrix (event-based edges)', '\\mathcal{L}': 'Laplacian matrix (graph structure)'}
primitives.assumptions: Graph structure is static per match; node features are time-invariant; edge types are predefined and semantically meaningful.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When graph connectivity is sparse or node features are missing, leading to underfitting or poor generalization.

layer2.mapping: Maps player and team interaction semantics to a shared latent space where outcomes are predicted via contrastive difference in team embeddings.

primitives.name: Team Interaction Network
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Team Interaction Network.** Directed graph over teams; edges = historical head-to-head **winning rate** (retain only the higher-rate directed edge, e.g., 20/30 → edge A→B valued 2/3).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{T}_{ij}': 'Normalized win rate from team i to j (dimensionless)', 'W_{ij}': 'Number of wins by team i against j', 'L_{ij}': 'Number of losses by team i against j'}
primitives.assumptions: Historical win rates are stable and informative; team performance does not change drastically between seasons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When teams have insufficient head-to-head data or when performance trends reverse.

layer2.mapping: Encodes team dominance as a kernel in the graph adjacency matrix for downstream transformer processing.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of win rate prediction on unseen matchups.

primitives.name: Match Comparison Transformer
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Match Comparison Transformer.** Player embeddings approximated pre-match by average pooling over last **T = 10** historical matches (empirically chosen over 5/10/20).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{z}_i^{\\text{avg}}': 'Average player embedding over T historical matches (dimension 16)', '\\mathbf{z}_i^{(t)}': 'Player embedding at time t (dimension 16)', 'T': 'Number of historical matches (fixed at 10)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player form is temporally consistent; recent matches are more predictive than older ones.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player form is volatile or when T is too small to capture variance.

layer2.mapping: Maps temporal player evolution into static pre-match embeddings for team-level comparison.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual match outcomes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in modeling heterogeneous interactions through a fusion of event-defined player graphs and historical team win rates. The transformer encodes both node and edge semantics using trainable embeddings and Laplacian eigenvectors, enabling expressive graph representation learning. The MoE gating mechanism allows dynamic weighting of global vs. local player features, improving adaptability. The team interaction network introduces a directed graph of win rates that acts as a prior on team strength. The match comparison transformer pools historical player embeddings to approximate pre-match states. Training proceeds in two stages: first, the graph encoders are pre-trained on match outcomes, then the gating and team components are fine-tuned. This modular design enables robust prediction while maintaining interpretability. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited data, incorrect edge semantics, or misalignment between historical and current team dynamics.
